1.1 Explain why and how the cloud is revolutionizing businesses

A regional retailer buys new servers every five years. Each refresh ties up a large amount of cash, and the servers sit mostly idle except during the holiday season, when they still run out of capacity. Which benefit of cloud technology most directly addresses both problems?
Longer hardware warranties from the cloud provider.
Pay-as-you-go pricing combined with on-demand scalability.
Dedicated physical servers in the provider's data center.
Paying only for what is used removes the large upfront purchase, and scaling on demand adds capacity for the holiday peak and releases it afterward.
Open-source licensing, warranties, and dedicated servers don't solve either the idle-capacity cost or the peak shortfall.
1.1 Explain why and how the cloud is revolutionizing businesses
Which statement best defines digital transformation?
Moving all servers to a colocation facility.
Buying the latest laptops for every employee.
Using new digital technologies to create or modify business processes, culture, and customer experiences to meet changing business and market needs.
Replacing paper forms with PDF files.

A media company wants to avoid being locked into a single vendor's proprietary technology so it can move workloads or combine tools from different providers in the future. Which Google Cloud differentiator speaks most directly to this concern?

1.1 Explain why and how the cloud is revolutionizing businesses
What is the difference between open source and an open standard?
They are two names for the same thing.
Open source software is always free of charge, while open standards are always paid.
Open source means the software's source code is publicly available to use and modify; an open standard is a publicly available specification that different vendors can implement.
Open standards apply only to hardware, and open source applies only to networking.
Open source refers to code that anyone can inspect, use, and modify under its license, while an open standard is a shared specification that many products can follow so they interoperate.
They're related but distinct, and neither is limited by cost or to one kind of technology.

A logistics company's competitors are launching new digital services every few weeks, while it takes the company six months just to provision servers for a new project. Executives ask what risk they face if they don't adopt the cloud. What is the best answer?

A regulatory requirement that blocks all cloud use.
Common organizational challenges of digital transformation, such as culture change and skills gaps.

A global news site experiences sudden traffic spikes during breaking news. It wants the site to stay fast and available for readers worldwide without buying servers in every country. Which cloud benefits apply?

Lower data quality and fewer analytics options.

1.1 Explain why and how the cloud is revolutionizing businesses

An insurance company currently spends most of its IT budget maintaining hardware and patching servers. The CEO wants IT staff to spend more time building products that differentiate the company. Which cloud benefit addresses this?
Strategic value and focus: managed services shift undifferentiated maintenance work to the provider, freeing staff for higher-value work.
Increased need for on-site hardware technicians.
Using managed cloud services means the provider handles much of the infrastructure maintenance, so teams can focus on innovation.
The other options increase or preserve the maintenance burden.

A healthcare startup wants to train and run large AI models but doesn't want to assemble specialized hardware itself. It wants a provider whose infrastructure is optimized for AI, from accelerators to software. Which Google Cloud differentiator best matches this need?
Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer, an integrated system of AI-optimized hardware, software, and flexible consumption models.
AI Hypercomputer combines accelerators such as TPUs and GPUs with optimized software and flexible consumption options for AI workloads.
Workspace is a productivity suite, Archive storage is for long-term data retention, and billing reports track spending.
1.1 Explain why and how the cloud is revolutionizing businesses

A retail chain collects sales, inventory, and customer data in separate systems. Leadership wants to use this data to predict demand and personalize offers. Which benefit of cloud technology does this describe?

In the context of cloud computing, what does "infrastructure" refer to?
Only the end-user applications employees use.
The physical and virtual resources, such as compute, storage, and networking, that applications run on.
Infrastructure is the foundational compute, storage, and networking resources that support applications and services.
Marketing, applications alone, and the org chart aren't infrastructure.

A government agency must keep certain sensitive workloads in its own data center for regulatory reasons, but wants to use the public cloud for new citizen-facing apps and analytics. Which cloud architecture fits?
A hybrid cloud combines on-premises (or private cloud) environments with public cloud, letting regulated workloads stay on-premises while other workloads use the public cloud.
Public-only or private-only doesn't meet both needs, and SaaS is a service model rather than an architecture.
A company uses Google Cloud for analytics and AI, another provider for its existing ERP system, and a third provider for email. What is this arrangement called?
Multicloud means using services from more than one public cloud provider, often to use each provider's strengths or reduce dependency on one vendor.
Private cloud and on-premises refer to dedicated environments, and edge computing places compute near users or devices.

A software company wants to run its own application code without managing operating systems, patching servers, or configuring the runtime, while still controlling the application itself. Which cloud service model fits best?
PaaS provides a managed platform where customers deploy their code while the provider manages the underlying servers and runtime.
IaaS requires managing operating systems, SaaS delivers finished software rather than hosting your code, and on-premises means managing everything.

A small business needs email, documents, and calendars for its employees. It has no IT staff and wants to simply use the software through a browser with no installation or maintenance. Which service model fits?
SaaS delivers complete applications over the internet, with the provider managing everything behind them.
IaaS and PaaS require the customer to build or manage applications, and bare metal requires managing hardware.
A research lab needs full control over virtual machines, including the operating system and installed software, but doesn't want to own physical hardware. Which service model and trade-off apply?
PaaS, with no access to the application code.
IaaS, with the most control over the environment but also the most management responsibility among cloud service models.
SaaS, with the least control and the least management effort.

IaaS gives customers control of virtual machines and operating systems while the provider manages physical infrastructure, which means more flexibility but more responsibility for patching and configuration.
SaaS and PaaS give less control, and on-premises requires owning hardware.
How do Google Cloud regions and zones relate to each other?
Regions and zones are the same thing.
A region is a specific geographic area made up of multiple zones, which are isolated deployment areas within that region.
Zones exist only for networking, and regions exist only for storage.
A region is a geographic location, and each region contains several zones, so deploying across zones protects against a failure in one zone.
Zones don't contain regions, the terms aren't interchangeable, and both apply to many kinds of resources.
An online video platform wants to keep its service running even if a single data center facility within a region fails. What should it do?
Deploy the application in only one zone with larger servers.
Deploy the application across multiple zones in the region.
Move to a single on-premises server room.
Spreading resources across multiple zones keeps the service available if one zone has a problem.
Bigger servers in one zone still share a single point of failure, laptop backups aren't a resilience strategy, and a single server room adds risk.

Users of a gaming app in Australia complain that the game feels slow, because every action has to travel to servers in North America and back. Which networking term describes the delay they experience?
Latency is the time it takes for data to travel from one point to another, and it increases with distance.
Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be transferred over time, DNS translates names to addresses, and an IP address identifies a device.
A company's website serves large images to visitors worldwide. It wants content cached closer to users to reduce load times. Which part of Google's network infrastructure helps most?
Edge locations (points of presence) that cache and deliver content close to users.
A single zone in one region.
Google's edge locations around the world, used by services such as Cloud CDN, cache content near users to reduce latency.
A single zone keeps content far from many users, office Wi-Fi is irrelevant, and DNS alone doesn't cache content.
